sections.heading: Modified Bitumen vs. TPO and EPDM: Benefits and Disadvantages of Bitumen Roofing

c.v: The benefits of modified bitumen roofing

runs.v: are redundancy and toughness: this durable, long lasting roofing system has served low-slope roofs for decades, offers long term durability against foot traffic, punctures, and weathering on commercial buildings with rooftop equipment, performs well in freezing temperatures, withstands harsh weather, and is cost-efficient with low upkeep, which is why New Jersey roofers often recommend it for the state's climate. Localized damage can be repaired without replacing the entire roof, and a reflective cap sheet makes it more energy efficient. The disadvantages: torch application carries fire risk, seams depend on the craft of the crew, the assembly is heavier and slower to install than single-ply materials, and dark cap sheets absorb heat unless coated. TPO is lighter, white, and heat-welded, best where energy efficiency on a large open deck matters, while modified bitumen tends to perform better under foot traffic, equipment service, and cold; EPDM usually costs less than modified bitumen. Property owners choose among these roofing solutions by traffic, sun, budget, and fire-safety limits, and an inspection and a written estimate help you make an informed decision about long-term performance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SBS and APP modified bitumen for a Montclair roof?

runs.v: SBS-modified bitumen holds low-temperature flexibility and resists cold cracking better than APP-modified bitumen, which runs heat-resistant and UV-stable but stiffer in cold. Newark Quality Roofing installs SBS modified bitumen for the Essex County freeze-thaw climate, per ARMA modified-bitumen guidance.

faqs.q: Is torch-applied modified bitumen safe on my occupied Montclair home?

runs.v: On occupied homes and tree-lined lots, Newark Quality Roofing applies self-adhered SBS or cold-adhesive membrane instead of a torch; where a torch is used, it follows NRCA hot-work protocol with fire extinguishers and a post-application fire watch.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for modified bitumen roofing in Montclair?

runs.v: A roof-covering replacement on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, so confirm with the Montclair construction office.

faqs.q: Does a modified bitumen roof in a Montclair historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can, mainly when the work changes a building's appearance; properties in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Montclair construction office before work. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: How long does a modified bitumen roof last in Montclair?

runs.v: Modified bitumen lasts 20 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, against EPDM at 15 to 25 years and TPO at 7 to 20 years; drainage and flashing detail set its realized lifespan.
